description: Representative raw prompts with objective, computed expectations for scorePrompt and lintPrompt. Every expected value in this file was produced by running the real functions, and promptCorpus.test.js asserts them back, so scoring or lint changes fail loudly instead of drifting.
selectionCriteria: Span the full scorePrompt range: at least one case at each points value from 1 to 5.
Span the lint range: at least one case firing no rules and one firing every rule.
Isolate each scorePrompt signal (role, task, format, constraints, context) in at least one case where it is the only one present.
Include a templated prompt so extractVars is exercised.
Contain no user data, no credentials, and no provider-specific text — every case is synthetic and safe to run anywhere.

cases.title: Bare task fragment
cases.rationale: Floor case. A task verb and nothing else — the weakest input the editor should still score rather than reject.

cases.title: Role with no task
cases.rationale: Isolates the role signal. Scores the same single point as a bare task, which is what makes points alone insufficient as a quality verdict.
cases.prompt: You are a senior technical editor.

cases.title: Constraints with no task or role
cases.rationale: Isolates the constraints signal, and is the case that fires goal_near_top and output_format without firing the constraints rule.
cases.prompt: Do not use jargon. Avoid passive voice. Must stay under 200 words.

cases.title: Format directive with nothing else
cases.rationale: Isolates the format signal, and is the only case that specifies a format without a goal — so it fires goal_near_top and constraints but not output_format.

cases.title: Long unstructured prose
cases.rationale: Worst-case lint: long enough to be non-trivial but with no role, goal, format, or constraints, so it fires all four rules. Isolates the context signal.
cases.prompt: The quarterly planning document needs a summary that captures the major themes discussed across the three workshops, including the disagreements that were not resolved, so that people who could not attend can catch up quickly without reading the full transcript of every session.

cases.title: Clear task, no structure
cases.rationale: The common real-world midpoint: the user says what they want but gives no role, format, or limits.
cases.prompt: Write a changelog entry for the release we shipped yesterday covering the API changes.

cases.title: Strict JSON contract
cases.rationale: Lint-clean without a role, proving a prompt can satisfy every lint rule while still scoring mid-range. Isolates the format signal.
cases.prompt: Return JSON only. Goal: extract every date. Format: {"dates": ["YYYY-MM-DD"]}. Do not add commentary.

cases.title: Templated prompt with variables
cases.rationale: Exercises extractVars alongside scoring, and covers the reusable-template shape the Library stores.
cases.prompt: You are a {{role}}. Goal: rewrite {{input_text}} for a {{audience}} audience. Respond in markdown. Do not exceed {{max_words}} words.

cases.title: Complete well-formed prompt
cases.rationale: Ceiling case. Every scorePrompt signal present and no lint rule fired — the target a successful enhance should reach.
cases.prompt: You are a senior release manager. Goal: produce a changelog entry for this release. Write it as a markdown bulleted list grouped by surface. Do not invent version numbers, and never include internal ticket IDs. Limit to eight bullets.
